findings.summary: The unsealed-case bullet calls the abandoned-unsealed-chain mechanism 'itself the M4.16/ADR-0029 defect class, now closed by M4.32' and hedges only for chains written before that fix. But the backlog's own M4.32 row says its fix shares `neverOpened`'s origin caveat and explicitly leaves 'an immediate predecessor that is WHOLLY empty (no CONTINUE, no Seal at all)' unwalked, tracked as M4.23 -- still `todo`. So M4.32 narrowed the M4.16 defect class, it did not close it: a new (not merely pre-existing) unsealed-and-undetected ancestor is still producible going forward through the M4.23 gap. 'now closed' overstates what the tree's own tracked state supports.
findings.failure_scenario: A future reader relying on this ADR to reason about how much residual exposure the unsealed-adoption gap carries concludes the M4.16 mechanism itself is fully retired and stops looking for it, when M4.23 (todo) describes a live, different route to the same unsealed-ancestor shape that M4.32 does not cover.
